empires.name: The Kingdoms of India
empires.note: War elephants walk through a shield wall like it is standing wheat. Panic one and it rampages into whoever stands nearest - as often their line as yours.

places.name: Pataliputra
places.note: The throne. Timber walls, sixty-four gates, a moat you could lose an army in.

places.name: Varanasi
places.note: Silk, dye-vats and pilgrims packed on the riverbank; the guards are used to crowds, not raids.

places.name: Ujjayini
places.note: Every western road meets here, and the tolls sit in the treasury between escorts.

places.name: Takshashila
places.note: The northern gate of the realm - everything that comes down from the passes is counted here first.

places.name: Mathura
places.note: Horse fair on the Yamuna; whoever holds it remounts an army in a week.

places.name: Pratishthana
places.note: Black rock and cattle in thousands, and no wall worth the name.

places.name: Tamralipti
places.note: The delta's warehouse town - goods stacked waiting on a road one day's march long.

places.name: Madurai
places.note: So far south that relief is three months away; the pearl merchants pay the temple and the temple pays no one.

places.name: Kaushambi
places.note: River market on an old fort - the ditch silted up two reigns ago.

empires.name: The Kingdom of the Nile
empires.note: Chariots run you down on open flat ground, so keep to broken country. The river feeds their army all year, and every town along it is fatter than anything you have burned.

places.name: Waset
places.note: The throne, which foreigners call Thebes. Stone pylons, vaults of temple gold, and priests who keep armed men of their own.

places.name: Men-nefer
places.note: White walls where the valley opens into the delta; every road north and south runs through it.

places.name: Alexandria
places.note: Straight streets and granaries the size of hills, held by hired foreigners paid in grain.

places.name: Abdju
places.note: A burial town - what is under the ground here is worth more than what walks on it.

places.name: Abu
places.note: The frontier at the cataract; the river turns to rock and the fort watches the desert road.

places.name: Per-Bastet
places.note: Festival crowds and fat temple herds, on soft delta ground cut through with canals.

places.name: Berenike
places.note: Where the desert road stops at the Red Sea - ivory and incense in sheds, a dozen guards.

places.name: Nekhen
places.note: Half sunk in sand; the priests are rich and the walls are mud brick.
